Esthíl (B54)

Scoring-table region: Escann.

In a sentence: Begin as the Order of the Iron Sceptre, turn necromancy from forbidden study into a national production system, and ultimately face all of Escann from a flying fortress as a Dark Empire of mages.

Story: Very high | Mission tree: Long (31 direct missions, excluding the predecessor's general adventurer missions) | Mission-tree update: the current rework file was updated through 2026-07-09 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Very high

Who are you actually playing?

Esthíl is not on the 1444 map. You begin as the Order of the Iron Sceptre (B20), an Escanni adventurer company led by mages; its ruler Aldres is a powerful mage. After the Greentide destroyed old Escann, the company entered the ruined lands not only to restore a country, but also to escape the Mage Council's restrictions on dangerous research. Once it completes its adventurer settlement phase, the Order can form Esthíl (B54), switch to 31 dedicated missions, and initialise the Necroeconomics system.

The offline Wiki describes Esthíl as a mage state led by Varina Escer and descended from the Order of the Iron Sceptre, and identifies the War of the Black Tower as a defining event. Its Escann overview likewise presents Esthíl as a mage regime born when an adventurer company became a state. Keep the timelines distinct: the current game files establish the Order's identity and its 1444 opening; the Wiki's later wars and 1663 destruction belong to the setting's historical timeline, not to an inevitable player-campaign ending.

What kind of national story is this?

The first half resembles an academic revolution spiralling out of control. Varina collects forbidden necromantic works, organises a Necromancer's Coven, and combines necromancy with disciplines such as divination and transmutation. The initial rationale sounds almost modern: the living should not die in mines, fields, and vast construction projects when the dead neither tire nor need wages. Orc and goblin corpses are first treated as labour; then come dedicated Harvest Fields, Dead Mines, and work crews to rebuild Castonath.

The true turning point is not whether necromancy is used, but whether the state declares the dead, their souls, and their corpses to be resources for allocation. Esthíl gradually creates a Death Tax, quotas for the dead, and a mage bureaucracy, using the dead to subsidise food, mining, industry, and the army. Opponents face coercion, purges, and reanimation. The mission tree moves steadily from a technical ideal of improving life toward a totalitarian mage state sustained by undead labour.

The second half turns the domestic experiment into a continental war. Esthíl seizes resources, destroys Carkinandar as a symbol of the opposing order, and builds the flying fortress Morgurax. The War of the Black Tower brings internal defections and an external coalition war at once, demanding that you hold the heartland at the worst possible moment. After the ordeal, Varina and her inner circle of necromancers pursue immortality, and the country openly embraces its identity as a Dark Empire: the living prosper, the dead perform all labour, and opponents of this order become the next workforce.

The mechanics that define the campaign

  1. Necroeconomics magic project: Form Esthíl and advance its missions to unlock a dedicated tier-three project. It is not just a permanent modifier; it has its own resources and progression.
  2. Allocating the dead: A dedicated interface allocates the dead between labourers and soldiers, and directs resources to construction, development, Harvest Fields, and Dead Mines. You are managing a second population economy.
  3. Mage state and Varina: The mage estate, magical research, and Varina's path to lichdom run through the campaign. High magic is an engine of governance and narrative, not a decorative bonus.
  4. Morgurax and repression: The flying fortress combines magical engineering, military intimidation, and domestic control, making it the campaign's clearest mid-to-late-game symbol.
  5. War of the Black Tower: This is the mission tree's final examination. External enemies, internal fracture, and a long general war convert all your earlier preparation into survival. Without it, the crisis can break you.

How a campaign tends to unfold

The opening is still a classic Escanni adventurer campaign: migrate, clear nearby territory, choose where to settle, and prepare the land needed to form Esthíl. The Order's powerful mage gives it formidable early wars, but the adventurer economy and rapid expansion also create financial and manpower pressure.

After forming Esthíl, the loop becomes: expand for corpses and resources; use the necroeconomy to strengthen the core; then use magic and industry to fuel the next expansion. You need both broad territory and a highly developed heartland, so this is neither pure map-painting nor a quiet tall campaign. Before the War of the Black Tower, preserve cash and manpower, build defensive depth with forts, and address diplomatic isolation. The common community-reported failure is not losing ordinary wars, but mistaking a pre-crisis snowball for having already won.

Formable successor and campaign boundary

This entry covers the continuous B20 Order of the Iron Sceptre → B54 Esthíl campaign. Esthíl may also form Black Demesne (Z99) once eligible; that changes the Tag and replaces the mission tree. The scoring table treats Black Demesne as a separate country, so its full content is not folded into this article. Esthíl's own climax is the War of the Black Tower, Morgurax, and its transformation into a Dark Empire. Forming Z99 continues into a different campaign.

Personality, values, and who should play it

The v2.1 personality profile is Expansion 90/100 | Autocracy 98/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 100/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 100/100) | Pluralism 10/100. The phase profiles are Order_of_the_Iron_Sceptre_early (Autocracy 65, Pluralism 35) → Esthil_late (Autocracy 98, Pluralism 10).

The v2.1 values profile is Evil (10/100), with a radicalising trajectory. Phase values are Order_of_the_Iron_Sceptre_early (Neutral 55/100) → Esthil_necroeconomy (Evil 25/100) → Esthil_late (Evil 10/100). The early ideal—'let the dead labour so the living can prosper'—has a public-benefit aspect. The main story progressively institutionalises killing orcs and goblins for labour, the Death Tax, exploitation of souls, purges, and rule by terror; this is therefore a clear radicalisation. Phase values: Order_of_the_Iron_Sceptre_early (Neutral 55/100) → Esthil_necroeconomy (Evil 25/100) → Esthil_late (Evil 10/100).

Recommended for players who enjoy dark narratives, powerful magic systems, a mix of development and conquest, and preparing for a major endgame crisis. If you dislike coerced atrocities, a complex resource interface, diplomatic isolation, or winning the first half only to face a general war, Esthíl will be punishing.

Community impressions

Players reviewing the current rework generally praise its atmosphere, magic system, and story of an idealistic project sliding into tyranny, while describing it as a high-intensity, aggressive, long Escanni campaign. Discussion centres on the War of the Black Tower: some say it finally gives purpose to all the preparation, while others find its warnings insufficient and the combination of internal fracture and an external coalition overwhelming. These posts describe player experience; they do not establish mission conditions or mechanic values, which remain grounded in the current local scripts.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Esthíl (B54) — Esthíli Ideas

Set ID: B54_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B54
    }

Esthíli Traditions

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

1. Sanctum for Outlawed Magisters

With the outbreak of the Greentide, vast swathes of land across Escann have been ruined. Were it not for the selfless acts of the brave magisters, in defiance of the Magisterium, the Greentide would have surely overcome all of Cannor. Esthíl itself has been established by these outlawed magisters, and it is with open arms that we accept any and all magic users who wish to join our realm.

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Possible advisors: +2 (advisor_pool; raw value 2).

2. Arcane Dawn

Throughout the lands of Cannor, magic is seen as a force that acts behind closed doors, in secret. That is not so for Esthíl. This is an Arcane Dawn for the world, when all may practice magic freely without fear of repercussion.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

3. Esthíli Academy of Magic

The Esthíli Academy of Magic is the foremost magical education institution in all of Escann. While there are those elsewhere who pretend to compete with our title, such as the Núrcestirans, all know that only the most elite of candidates are accepted and graduate from Esthíl.

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

4. Sanctioned Necromancy

The Magisterium foolishly all but banned necromancy, one of the most powerful schools of magic. It is only fitting that we should sanction its usage as the other schools of magic are treated, for a loyal necromancer can bring many boons to our nation. Besides free manual labor, the necromancer themselves would remain loyal to the one cause that permits them.

  • Yearly corruption: -0.05 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.05).

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

5. Grimoire of Tenebral Secrets

A horrid manuscript found in a long-forgotten vault, the Grimoire of Tenebral Secrets lives up to its name. It bestows great power to those who can read and understand it, but at the risk of immediate death if not worthy.

  • All estates' loyalty equilibrium: +5% (all_estate_loyalty_equilibrium; raw value 0.05).

6. Mystic Vaults of Castle Esthíl

Far below the shadowy and ominous Castle Esthíl, the Mystic Vaults are a vast labyrinth filled with countless magical artifacts and spellbooks. From far and wide magical artifacts are tithed to fill the ever-expanding needs of the elite magisters.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

7. Elementary Magical Education for the Soldiery

Previously the domain of melee, volley or the occasional magical blast, warfare has now changed. With the advent of a new technique, all of our soldiers can be equipped with the ability to cast minor spells. All shall fear the might of Esthíl!

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

Esthíli Ambition

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

Black Demesne (Z99) — Black Demesner Ideas

Set ID: Z99_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z99 #Black Demesne
    }

Black Demesner Tradition

  • shock_damage_received: -20% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.2).

  • Siege ability: +20% (siege_ability; raw value 0.2).

1. The Ascendant

In the cosmology of the Black Doctrine, all beings with the capability to use magic are positioned somewhere in a great chain of ascension, sometimes called the 'Ascendant Path'. At the near end of this path are the so-called 'potentiates', people who have latent magical ability but lack the discipline to use it in any consistent and meaningful way. At the far end lies the Universal Mind, the great dispassionate, impersonal intellect which suffuses all the world. The Ascendant is the being who traverses this great path, growing in each stage until they achieve a true union with that purest Intellect. Officially, every Sorcerer-King was Ascendant, though any serious discussion with heretics will reveal that this is a point of much contention.

  • Maximum Absolutism: +20 (max_absolutism; raw value 20).

2. The Week of Ascension

The Week of Ascension was simultaneously one of the world's most egalitarian institutions and one of its most stratified. Regardless of social class, all non-magical subjects participated in the same festivals and shared in the same activities during the seven-day celebration of virtue. However, every magic user was kept separate from these festivities, instead joining the Sorcerer-King in the Charred Tower for a week of celebration, debauchery, and furious politicking.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

3. Unrestricted Magic

There have been various attempts to regulate and control magical research throughout the history of the mortal realms. Indeed, perhaps one of the truest signs of a healthy state has been its ability to impose at least some basic restrictions on the activities of mages. In the Black Demesne, to suggest such regulations was not merely seen as foolish, but rather a blasphemous heresy against Doctrine itself. Any law which restricted the development of Intellect was opposed to Doctrine, and restrictions on magic were the most heinous of these.

  • All power costs: -5% (all_power_cost; raw value -0.05).

4. In the Eyes of the Great

Though the non-magical classes could not ascend to the highest rungs of state power in the Demesne, and though they had very limited rights, they nonetheless rose in prominence. Precisely because the most powerful positions were restricted to magic users, these same powerful people often chose to surround themselves with those who could not possibly be a threat. They often promoted members of the non-magical class based on pure competence, justifying the high placement on the basis of intellectual virtue. This was in stark contrast to many other kingdoms, where promotion was by right of blood alone.

  • Years of separatism: -5 (years_of_nationalism; raw value -5).

5. The Reaper's Gift

Undead are useful on the field of battle as brute soldiers, but they have very limited capacity to think for themselves or listen to verbal orders. Thus, the Demesne had great need for living scouts, battlefield engineers, and officers. Such positions were an excellent way for non-magical subjects to climb the social ladder by making themselves valuable to mages. Every time war was declared, a great influx of some of the Demesne's most intelligent, driven, and ambitious people came to serve the army in all manner of roles, a pattern that would later earn the moniker of 'the Reaper's Gift'.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

6. Reformulated Organization

In most societies, mages are typically reclusive academics who have little interest in battlefield glory, and only a smaller portion have the inclination to take up arms and lend their talents to the field of glory. In the Demesne, it was an expectation and personal obligation for every magical initiate to serve for at least some time in the military. This vastly greater pool of magical manpower allowed the Demesne to turn the entire upper officer corps into the exclusive province of mages, allowing decentralized and responsive magical tactics that were far more impressive than any single sorcerer could achieve alone.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Mages Influence: +10% (mages_influence_modifier; raw value 0.1).

7. Rings of the Eight

At its greatest extent, the Black Demesne had eight Acolytes, each of whom wore an ebony ring, numbered from the First to the Eighth in order of magical prowess and prominence within the court. The Sorcerer-King wore a matching ring of dark gold, signifying dominance, which would become known as the Ninth ring. Theoretically, as long as one wore the ring of an Acolyte, one was honorbound to give nothing but absolute loyalty to the legitimate bearer of the Ninth ring in all matters. This reminder of hierarchy and control fortified the political order of the Demesne's upper class.

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +10% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Liberty Desire in Subjects on the Same Continent: +1500% (reduced_liberty_desire_on_same_continent; raw value 15).

Black Demesner Ambition

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).
